profile.name: Harbor
profile.subtitle: Energy · housing · workforce
profile.question: Which investments can cut household energy burden without displacing residents?
profile.context: A fictional regional compact covers 1,200 occupied homes and a constrained district energy network. The compact has a $60 million appropriation, a 36-month projection, two municipal partners and an independent resident assembly. Procurement quotes, consent records and workforce estimates disagree. The figures below are synthetic planning proxies, not an engineering assessment.
profile.authority: Harbor compact board; resident assembly consent is required for work in occupied homes.
principles: Resident consent can be withdrawn before work begins.
Regional emissions must not rise above the starting estimate.
Treat contested estimates as revisable claims, not commitments.

scopes.name: Harbor compact
scopes.description: Two municipalities coordinate an appropriation of $60 million over 36 months. Neither owns the resident assembly nor the training college.

scopes.name: District network
scopes.description: Substation commissioning and heat-network work share scarce electrical crews. Utility consent does not authorize entry into homes.

scopes.name: Occupied housing
scopes.description: 1,200 homes; 480 currently meet the compact's winter comfort threshold. Tenants retain separate consent rights.

scopes.name: Skills partnership
scopes.description: The college and two unions can certify additional installers; training hours cannot substitute for qualified crew hours.

scopes.name: Resident assembly
scopes.description: An independent institution representing residents in both municipalities. Consent is bounded by the signed register, not assumed from participation.

scopes.name: Transition fund
scopes.description: The appropriation funds complete packages. Unspent authority is available for contingencies; it is not additional capacity.

objectives.label: Emissions
objectives.description: Synthetic annual regional energy emissions index. Reductions add as a planning approximation; rebound and interactions remain outside this first model.

objectives.label: Warm homes
objectives.description: Occupied homes expected to meet the winter comfort threshold. A home is counted once within each proposed package; forecasts cannot exceed the 1,200-home stock.

objectives.label: Qualified installers
objectives.description: People with the agreed safety certification; forecast completion is not an employment guarantee.

objectives.label: Involuntary moves
objectives.description: A protected limit, independent of financial or carbon benefits. Any planned involuntary move makes a portfolio inadmissible.

objectives.label: Energy burden
objectives.description: Median modeled household energy expenditure as a share of disposable income. Tariff and technical savings are uncertain, additive proxies.

source.title: Tender reconciliation · synthetic

claims.dissent: The infrastructure committee expects a 1.5 index once road permissions are priced.

interventions.title: Commission the network
interventions.mechanism: Reserve transformer delivery and commission the district connection before dependent housing work begins.

interventions.title: Treat the winter cohort
interventions.mechanism: Insulate and rebalance 80 consenting homes with current qualified crews; retain a measured comparison cohort.

interventions.title: Certify the next cohort
interventions.mechanism: Fund 90 opt-in trainees through the college and union certification pathway; do not count their hours as crew capacity in this portfolio.

interventions.title: Retrofit 280 homes
interventions.mechanism: Combine insulation, ventilation and heat-pump work after network commissioning and certification. Only separately reserved crew hours supply the work.

interventions.title: Build the shared heat loop
interventions.mechanism: Connect a separate 240-home consenting cohort to district heat after commissioning. Road-crossing cost remains contested.

interventions.title: Offer a resident tariff
interventions.mechanism: Enroll a separate 120-household cohort in a voluntary tariff with a capped winter price. Enrolment and exit remain opt-in.

interventions.title: Clear and rebuild the block
interventions.mechanism: A developer proposes demolition and fast replacement. The proposal entails 22 involuntary moves and conflicts with the compact's protected resident limit.

strategies.name: Winter first
strategies.thesis: Build evidence and skills while relieving immediate bills. Preserve capital and avoid committing to the contested network window.

strategies.name: Homes and skills
strategies.thesis: Commit to a deeper 280-home transition, contingent on network commissioning. Reserve the full work package before agents begin.

strategies.name: Build everything
strategies.thesis: Test the advertised fast transformation against shared resources and resident protections. High modeled benefits cannot override either constraint.

shocks.name: Crews allocated elsewhere
shocks.description: The neighboring region accepts the overlapping contractor offer. Our confirmed qualified crew allocation falls from 18,000 to 9,500 hours.

shocks.name: Transformer slot lost
shocks.description: A vendor notice moves commissioning to month 30. Dependent housing work finishes after the 36-month projection and contributes no benefit inside it.

profile.name: Meridian
profile.subtitle: Manufacturing · supply · resilience
profile.question: How do we restore reliable delivery without exhausting people or cash?
profile.context: A fictional manufacturer operates two plants and serves a concentrated customer base. A critical component supplier missed three delivery windows. Engineering hours, cash commitments and customer service compete across sites; reported machine capacity does not imply available skilled labor. All contracts and figures in this example are synthetic.
profile.authority: Meridian executive committee; plant councils retain the right to reject unsafe workload changes.
principles: Do not increase the recorded fatigue index.
Preserve at least $5 million of operating cash.
Do not increase the emissions estimate.
Separate quoted supplier performance from verified deliveries.

scopes.name: Meridian group
scopes.description: A 12-month recovery program allocates $18 million; plant teams and suppliers retain distinct authorities.

scopes.name: North plant
scopes.description: Produces the constrained component. Its technical team also supports the South plant; hours cannot be committed twice.

scopes.name: South plant
scopes.description: Assembly and final delivery depend on components from North and the external supplier.

scopes.name: Supplier network
scopes.description: Two candidate suppliers can qualify reserved lots; neither is owned by Meridian. Quoted lead times are contested.

scopes.name: Plant councils
scopes.description: Councils represent the two plants on workload and safety. Overtime is a proposed intervention, not an automatic resource.

objectives.label: On-time delivery
objectives.description: Modeled deliveries meeting the promised date. Portfolio effects use distinct customer cohorts and remain forecasts; rates above 100% are inadmissible.

objectives.label: Single-source exposure
objectives.description: Share of critical demand with only one qualified source. Qualification is a dependency, not presumed from an offer.

objectives.label: Fatigue
objectives.description: Synthetic workload and fatigue proxy, protected at the current value. A high delivery forecast cannot compensate for a violation.

objectives.label: Emissions
objectives.description: Estimated annual operating emissions. Changes in product mix and energy contracts need a later model revision.

objectives.label: Operating cash
objectives.description: Cash remaining after modeled working-capital effects. The investment appropriation is tracked separately; inventory ties up operating cash.

source.title: Capital committee minute · synthetic
source.author: Inez Rao
source.excerpt: The committee approved $18 million for the 12-month recovery package. This is separate from the $8 million working-capital baseline.

claims.label: Technical allocation

source.title: Cross-plant capacity reconciliation · synthetic
source.author: Malik Reed
source.excerpt: After current production commitments, the two plants list 16,000 technical hours for recovery work. A maintenance shutdown may claim 6,000 of those hours.

claims.dissent: South's maintenance team has not released its shutdown reservation.

source.title: Trial-cell reservation · synthetic
source.author: Rosa Kim
source.excerpt: 2,000 machine hours are reserved for tooling trials and efficiency validation. Technical labor remains a separate constraint.

source.title: Supplier reservation letters · synthetic

source.title: Energy contract allocation · synthetic
source.author: Rosa Kim
source.excerpt: The recovery program may consume up to 4,500 MWh of separately contracted trial energy. Carbon effects are evaluated independently.

claims.label: Supplier qualification lead

source.title: Qualification sequence · synthetic
source.author: Owen Shah
source.excerpt: The supplier quotes three months of qualification after the component audit. Its test laboratory slot is provisional.

claims.dissent: The laboratory has a twelve-month queue if the reserved slot is reassigned.

claims.label: Tooling price

source.title: Tooling quote · synthetic
source.author: Malik Reed
source.excerpt: The $6 million cell estimate uses a price ratio of 1.0. Imported fixtures and integration work are not fixed-price.

claims.dissent: The supplier has indicated a possible 80% increase after a currency move.

source.title: Qualification cohort estimate · synthetic
source.author: Owen Shah
source.excerpt: At a 0.75 response ratio, qualification is expected to recover 10 points of delivery reliability and remove 22 points of single-source exposure. Pilot lots have not reached final acceptance.

interventions.title: Audit the component chain
interventions.mechanism: Reconcile acceptance criteria, failure causes and two candidate supplier routes before qualification or tooling commitments.

interventions.title: Qualify a second supplier
interventions.mechanism: Validate 20 reserved lots against the audited criteria. Release production only after qualification closes.

interventions.title: Install a flexible cell
interventions.mechanism: Add an internally controlled component route after the audit. Commissioning consumes engineering and trial-machine time; quoted capacity alone is insufficient.

interventions.title: Cross-train plant teams
interventions.mechanism: Protect paid training time and redistribute qualified coverage. Training benefits are forecast outcomes, not newly available technical hours in the same plan.

interventions.title: Reduce process energy
interventions.mechanism: Validate heat recovery and standby controls without changing production acceptance standards.

interventions.title: Buy a buffer stock
interventions.mechanism: Reserve 45 accepted lots against near-term customer orders. The stock protects delivery but ties up operating cash and adds storage emissions.

interventions.title: Add an overtime shift
interventions.mechanism: A proposed additional shift raises forecast delivery at the cost of fatigue and energy use. The plant councils have not authorized it.

strategies.name: Qualify and train
strategies.thesis: Restore reliability through a second supplier and paid training. Depend on laboratory timing rather than a new internal asset.

strategies.name: Control the bottleneck
strategies.thesis: Invest in an internal cell, training and energy efficiency. Use more engineering capacity to gain control and lower emissions.

strategies.name: Recovery at any cost
strategies.thesis: Combine every requested measure. Expose overcommitted technical capacity, unsafe fatigue and depleted operating cash before authorization.

shocks.name: Laboratory slot lost
shocks.description: The external laboratory withdraws the provisional slot. Qualification now takes twelve months after the audit, beyond the recovery horizon.

shocks.name: Shutdown claims engineers
shocks.description: A required South-plant shutdown reserves 6,000 hours. Only 10,000 technical hours remain for the strategic recovery package.

profile.name: Open Atlas
profile.subtitle: Knowledge · institutions · commons
profile.question: How can a shared knowledge commons grow without losing consent or maintainability?
profile.context: A fictional federation of a public library, two research labs and a civic archive maintains openly reusable climate-adaptation material. Their memberships overlap but their permissions do not. Volunteer time is pledged and finite. The federation must choose between deeper verification and wider reuse; unpublished personal records cannot be traded for reach.
profile.authority: Open Atlas stewardship council; originating institutions retain publication rights and participants retain consent rights.
principles: No private personal record may be exposed.
Consent is specific, revocable and separate from institutional membership.
Do not create a maintenance burden above the present allocation.
Preserve open reuse and the ability to fork without central permission.

scopes.name: Open Atlas federation
scopes.description: An 18-month shared program has $1.2 million, bounded volunteer pledges and independent institutional commitments.

scopes.name: Public library
scopes.description: Hosts openly licensed materials and assists contributors. Hosting does not confer rights over unpublished records.

scopes.name: Research partnership
scopes.description: Two independent labs validate claims. Their reviewers also contribute to the archive; the same pledged hours cannot be allocated twice.

scopes.name: Civic archive
scopes.description: Holds adaptation records and unpublished oral histories. Only the specifically consented collection can enter the commons.

scopes.name: Contributor assembly
scopes.description: Contributors belong to several institutions but retain individual publication rights. Neither a lab nor the council can override withdrawal.

objectives.label: Reusable materials
objectives.description: Materials with an open license, usable metadata and an exportable file. Items are counted once across the selected work packages.

objectives.label: Verified claims
objectives.description: Share of the reference collection with a traceable evidence check. Forecast changes are percentage-point proxies, not guarantees of truth.

objectives.label: Rights resolved
objectives.description: Share of the reference collection with explicit reuse rights and a withdrawal route. A license alone does not establish participant consent.

objectives.label: Private records exposed
objectives.description: Protected limit on exposure of unpublished personal records. Aggregate openness cannot compensate for even one exposure.

objectives.label: Maintenance burden
objectives.description: Estimated recurring work after the program. Volunteer pledges cover program delivery; they do not silently absorb future maintenance.

source.title: Grant award · synthetic
source.author: Mina Sol
source.excerpt: The 18-month grant commits $1.2 million to federation work. Future fundraising is excluded from available funding.

claims.label: Opt-in volunteer time

source.title: Pledge reconciliation · synthetic
source.author: Tess Okoro
source.excerpt: Named, opt-in pledges total 2,400 hours after removing duplicate pledges across institutions. Contributors may withdraw unworked time.

claims.dissent: About 1,000 hours depend on a university term timetable that has not been confirmed.

source.title: Partner letters · synthetic
source.author: Samir Vale
source.excerpt: The library, labs and archive commit 800 paid hours for this program. The same staff listed in multiple letters were counted once.

source.title: Hosting allocation · synthetic
source.author: Dara Lin
source.excerpt: Partners reserve 20 TB including required replicated copies. Unfunded personal drives are not federation infrastructure.

source.title: Participant permission register · synthetic
source.author: Tess Okoro
source.excerpt: 180 record-specific provisional permissions are active. Openly licensed public reference material uses a separate rights review; no silent personal-record release is assumed.

claims.label: Verification lead

source.title: Review calendar · synthetic
source.author: Samir Vale
source.excerpt: The labs offer a four-month evidence review after catalog reconciliation. This relies on two named reviewers completing a separate public-health study.

claims.dissent: The current study could extend the queue to sixteen months.

source.title: Translation pilot estimate · synthetic
source.author: Dara Lin
source.excerpt: At the working response ratio of 0.8, translated bundles are expected to add 180 reusable items. Pilot readers have not yet checked technical accuracy.

source.title: Reviewer sample · synthetic
source.author: Samir Vale
source.excerpt: A small sample suggests a 0.9 response ratio, modeled as a 20-point increase in verified claims. Ambiguous claims must retain their contested status after review.

interventions.title: Reconcile the public catalog
interventions.mechanism: Deduplicate already-public materials, trace licenses and produce a shared exportable catalog before dependent work.

interventions.title: Review the reference claims
interventions.mechanism: Check the reconciled collection against dated evidence, retaining disagreement and provenance. Verification is a bounded review, not a declaration of universal truth.

interventions.title: Translate reusable bundles
interventions.mechanism: Translate distinct public technical materials after catalog reconciliation. Reader validation limits modeled reach; no personal records enter this package.

interventions.title: Resolve participant permissions
interventions.mechanism: Review 100 provisional permissions with contributors, separate private material from public files and establish an accessible withdrawal path.

interventions.title: Release the consented archive
interventions.mechanism: Publish a distinct permitted collection after catalog and consent review, with replicated files and no private-record exposure.

interventions.title: Publish a portable fork kit
interventions.mechanism: Package verified public material, schemas and offline tooling so independent institutions can reuse and leave the federation without asking central permission.

interventions.title: Import the entire archive
interventions.mechanism: A proposed bulk release would include 20 unpublished personal records and unresolved rights. Its apparent reach is inadmissible under the privacy protection.

strategies.name: Rights and evidence
strategies.thesis: Resolve publication rights and verify the existing collection before seeking scale. Leave capacity for contributors who withdraw.

strategies.name: Portable commons
strategies.thesis: Make reviewed public knowledge reusable across independent institutions. Favor portability and lower maintenance over expanding the personal archive.

strategies.name: Publish everything
strategies.thesis: Test the tempting reach-maximizing portfolio against volunteer pledges, institutional allocations, maintenance and private-record protection.

shocks.name: Pledges withdrawn
shocks.description: The university timetable changes and contributors withdraw 1,000 unworked hours. No agent may assume free replacement labor.

shocks.name: Evidence review delayed
shocks.description: Reviewers extend the public-health study. Verification takes sixteen months after catalog work; the dependent fork kit misses the program horizon.

decisions.authority: Open Atlas stewardship council; originating institutions retain publication rights and participants retain consent rights.
decisions.rationale: Resolve publication rights and verify the existing collection before seeking scale. Leave capacity for contributors who withdraw.
